shortlist.label: Gallbladder cancer
shortlist.why_kept: calcified gallbladder wall invading liver segments, consistent with gallbladder cancer

shortlist.label: Adenocarcinoma of the gallbladder
shortlist.why_kept: distended gallbladder with poor delineation of the posterior wall, large, solid, and heterogeneous with posterior dense shadowing and calcific components

shortlist.label: Hepatic metastases from colorectal cancer

shortlist.label: Cholangiocarcinoma

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a distended gallbladder with a large, solid, and heterogeneous mass, along with a history of a partially calcified gallbladder, and the CT findings of a 10-cm calcified gallbladder wall invading liver segments, are highly suggestive of gallbladder cancer. The presence of enlarged lymph nodes and multiple pulmonary nodules consistent with metastatic disease further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Adenocarcinoma of the gallbladder
rejected.why: This is a subtype of gallbladder cancer, and while it could be a possible diagnosis, the provided information does not specifically distinguish it from other types of gallbladder cancer.

rejected.label: Hepatic metastases from colorectal cancer
rejected.why: There is no mention of a primary colorectal cancer, and the findings are more consistent with a primary gallbladder malignancy.

rejected.label: Cholangiocarcinoma
rejected.why: The normal common bile duct calibre and lack of intrahepatic duct dilatation make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Porcelain gallbladder with cancer
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of a partially calcified gallbladder, the current findings are more indicative of an invasive cancer rather than a porcelain gallbladder, which is a condition characterized by extensive calcification of the gallbladder wall without necessarily implying the presence of cancer.
